title: Registry-growth: at what registry size does routing measurably beat the global fallback?
question: As the arm registry grows over synthetic families with distinct descriptors, at what size K does routed accuracy (with the registered eps-advance rule) measurably beat the global mean-predictor fallback?

interpretation_registered_before_running.gate: K* = the smallest registry size where mean margin >= 0.05 AND at least 2/3 of included families improve over the fallback
interpretation_registered_before_running.exclusion: a family is excluded from the margin where the best measured arm scores below 0.1 R2 (iid/noise families: routing cannot beat a fallback on noise; measuring there tests nothing). Applied uniformly across all K.
interpretation_registered_before_running.raw_nearest: the raw nearest-arm margin (no eps-advance) is reported alongside; the eps-advance rule is the registered deployment behavior
interpretation_registered_before_running.trigger: K* is the registered learned-router trigger size for the deployment-phase learned policy

cell.families: synthetic AR families over the axis grid: temporal {iid, sequential, delayed} x noise {low, medium, high} x stationarity {stationary, non-stationary}, interleaved assignment (temporal cycles fastest)

model.note: one self-consistent in-process encoder (the M172b pattern)
